# Bounded parameter-name validation

Prepared, not executed. Root reviews and freezes actual code before running
this driver. It imports the existing reviewed fixed validation code and keeps
its authored commands, explicit Rust versions, native identity, raw failure
records, capacities and eleven selected integration targets. No command is
executed from a stored observation or selection file. The wrapper and original
driver are included in the declared source input map; their bytes, not a hash
of a claimed Git HEAD, identify the observed code. The existing map remains an
incomplete build/fixture closure.

Run the latest mode first, capture the separate fixed before/after CLI
comparison without rebuilding, then run MSRV. The single target is
`/private/tmp/qleisli-bounded-validation-target`, jobs2, incremental0, debug0.
Latest is actual Homebrew Rust1.98.1; MSRV uses `rustup run 1.85.0 cargo`.
The wrapper's advisory lock covers these validation invocations only; root
coordinates every build and comparison using that target.

The inherited target selection exercises actual finite/sized parameters,
exact Unit/tuple shape, lexical identity, effects, unused declarations,
selected CLI and existing small independent native/reference checks. Three
existing sized tests remain ignored, and two unrelated 3000-file import-depth
tests are explicitly skipped. No maximum quantum input or full new differential
corpus is generated. Formatting, all-target compile and denied-warning Clippy
are separate from test execution; expected counts are not actual results.

This adds no native rule, public API, protected record, dependency or edition.
Both scoped QLV1 guarantees keep their premises. Passing these bounded checks
does not discharge broader QS/PR/RS/EXACT, source preservation, common checking,
namespace migration or same-commit release gates.
